family_member_contact_frequency_per_week.assessment: The patient was brought to the emergency department by his wife and son, suggesting ongoing involvement, but there is no explicit mention of contact frequency per week.

patient_age_value_recorded_inthehistory_.assessment: Dementia symptoms began six months ago; given the patient is 89, symptom onset was at approximately age 88.
patient_age_value_recorded_inthehistory_.evidence: "An 89-year-old man... after six months of progressive changes in cognition and personality"

patient_age_value_recorded_now_in_years.assessment: The patient is described as an 89-year-old man.
patient_age_value_recorded_now_in_years.evidence: "An 89-year-old man was brought to the emergency department..."

patient_has_diagnosis_of_aphasia_now.assessment: He had difficulty expressing himself and speech was fluent with similar-sounding word substitutions, indicating aphasia.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_aphasia_now.evidence: "difficulty expressing himself", "speech was fluent, but he often used similar-sounding word substitutions"

patient_has_family_member_with_regular_c.assessment: The wife and son are involved in his care and brought him to the hospital, but the frequency of contact is not specified.

patient_has_diagnosis_of_primary_progres.assessment: The patient has a fluent aphasia with paraphasic errors, but there is no explicit mention of a diagnosis of primary progressive aphasia or established progressive isolated language deficit.

patient_is_living_in_community_now.assessment: He was brought from home by family members; there is no mention of institutionalization or dementia-specific living facilities.
patient_is_living_in_community_now.evidence: "was brought to the emergency department by his wife and son" (implies community dwelling)

patient_is_living_in_dementia_specific_l.assessment: The chart specifies that the patient was brought to the emergency department by his wife and son and describes family caregiving at home, with no mention of residence in a dementia-specific, 24/7-manned living facility.
patient_is_living_in_dementia_specific_l.evidence: An 89-year-old man was brought to the emergency department by his wife and son...

patient_has_finding_of_alcohol_intake_ab.assessment: The chart does not mention alcohol intake or consumption; vignettes reliably state substance abuse if present.

patient_has_finding_of_amyotrophic_later.assessment: No mention of ALS, motor neuron disease, or findings suggestive thereof are present in the chart.

patient_has_diagnosis_of_cerebral_infarc.assessment: There is no mention or clinical inference of acute or chronic cerebral infarction.

patient_has_finding_of_complete_trisomy_.assessment: There is no mention or clinical inference of Down syndrome or trisomy 21.

patient_has_finding_of_dementia_associat.assessment: There is no mention of alcoholism or alcohol-related dementia; vignettes state substance abuse if present.
No specific mention of dementia being secondary to another disease (e.g., Huntington, HIV, Down syndrome).

patient_has_family_member_with_regular_c.assessment: The patient was brought to the ED by his wife and son; this implies active family contact and support.
patient_has_family_member_with_regular_c.evidence: The patient was brought to the emergency department by his wife and son.

patient_has_finding_of_frontal_lobe_synd.assessment: Chart describes progressive personality changes, disinhibition, and executive dysfunction, consistent with frontal lobe syndrome.
patient_has_finding_of_frontal_lobe_synd.evidence: Progressive changes in cognition and personality; unusual behaviors; cannot follow multi-step commands; frequently interrupted the examiner; repeatedly reached out to grab things.

patient_has_finding_of_frontal_lobe_synd.assessment: No evidence of motor neuron disease or ALS is described.
No evidence that frontal lobe dysfunction is due to non-progressive injury (e.g., stroke or trauma).

patient_has_finding_of_human_immunodefic.assessment: The chart contains no mention of HIV infection, testing, diagnosis, or related features; as an exclusion, per prescreen doctrine, silence defaults to FALSE.

patient_has_finding_of_huntington_s_chor.assessment: No mention of Huntington's disease or characteristic choreiform movements or family history; as an exclusion, per doctrine, silence defaults to FALSE.

patient_has_finding_of_intellectual_disa.assessment: No history or statements indicative of lifelong intellectual disability (mental retardation); acute cognitive decline described is not consistent with developmental intellectual disability; silence defaults to FALSE.

patient_has_finding_of_substance_misuse_.assessment: No mention of alcohol or drug misuse, dependence, or suspicion thereof; patient is elderly, living with family, and brought by family, without reported substance abuse patterns; silence defaults to FALSE.
